comments.text:
I knew this retirement crisis was coming 20 years ago, and I was in a horrible place.

My wife didn't work, I was the sole provider, and we lost our house to foreclosure in the 2008 recession.  Still, I managed to sock away about $225k in my 401k; however...

At 60, I was laid off from my company after 17 years there (a few years back).  It was expected.  Work was being automated, AI was emerging, Corporate preferred to hire from India, and every year benefits were reduced and pay raises shrunk to next to nothing.  So, I knew it was coming.  Here's what I did...

I bought a 5 acre property with a dry hunting cabin on it.  I installed solar panels, water storage tanks, and built the infrastructure to support living off grid.  We built raised garden beds, greenhouses, and planted fruit trees (all while I was still employed, and all with what the paycheck would afford without going into debt).

When my layoff came, we had already moved onto our property and lived in our "shack in the woods". 

The property was bought for only $65k, and we don't have a mortgage.  We also don't have home insurance payments because no company would cover this structure.  We drive paid off vehicles that are 12 or more years old.  We haul all of our own household trash to the dump every month (we built a large wooden dumpster to hold our trash) for about $10.  I have a special trailer with a pump that I use to haul all of our water onto the property, again for about $10-15 bucks a month.

We did hook up city power to our property so we can run heating and cooling, and our electrical bill tends to be our most expensive monthly bill.

We looked at modern life with all the insurances they convinced people that they needed, and this belief that a suburban life was the best way to live, and we rejected allnof that.

How did people live for hundreds and thousands of years before mortgages, insurance coverages, auto payments, and all these other "modern conveniences" and just try to live your life as simply as you can.  Learn to be your own contractor for everything (carpentry, plumbing, electrical, etc).  Build redundancies into your systems so you don't need to be insured.  Be self reliant instead.  Over the years I have over bought construction supplies, and I actually have enough materials on my property to build a tiny house or two if my current cabin burns down.  I have an old beat up RV that is my bug-out vehicle if SHTF.  During Covid, I used my Covid check to buy a year's worth of dehydrated meals, and we've been adding tonthis long term food supplies ever since.  If our country were to collapse, I think we'd be okay.  

My 401k is gone.  Had to use it to bridge the gap between when I was laid off at 60 until I could claim Social Security at 62.  I also used parts of my 401k to install my 400amp utility connection, and to install a septic system on our property.  However...  The Social Security check alone is supporting us now.  We're getting by, because we took the last few years of my working career to say:  "Let's prepare to live far more modestly than we ever thought we could because NO ONE is coming to save us".  

I work every day now.  Servicing my infrastructure, watering our  garden and orchard, and building and improving my property.  It is far better doing this than stand at the entrance of Walmart saying, "Welcome to Walmart".
